title: Data-ink ratio and removing visual noise

videos.script: This is a bar chart the way a spreadsheet often draws it. A grey background, a frame, a black grid, and a legend for its only series. {{before}} Now count what is on it. Six bars carry the data. Everything else is there to be looked past. {{count}} Take the background away. Then the frame. Make the grid faint, and then remove it, writing each value beside its bar. {{steps}} Nothing the reader needed has gone. The bars are easier to see, and one of them was partly hidden behind the legend. {{after}} Edward Tufte called this the data-ink ratio: the share of the ink that shows data. {{ratio}} This lesson measures it, removes the noise in a fixed order, and asks where to stop, because a chart with only its data cannot be read. {{plan}}
